statusText: Calm, wait-and-see conditions continue into the European morning ahead of today's Retail Sales / UMich data cluster. Overnight Asia was mildly constructive (Nikkei +0.7%, Kospi +0.9% on continued AI/chip strength) while Hang Seng lagged (-0.51%). Brent held little changed near $87.18 as markets stayed in a wait-and-see mode on diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz -- a U.S. official cited progress on an Iran-Oman deal, a mild de-escalatory signal versus Thursday's rhetoric, though Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority continues to publicly reject that the strait is open. VIX remains flat near 14.5-14.7. The S&P/Nasdaq futures levels surfaced by this run's search matched the prior run's figures almost exactly, indicating a stale/cached quote rather than a fresh intraday print; Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a sixth consecutive run, so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch, with no confirmed live futures price-path evidence this hour.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Continue monitoring through the European morning and into the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment cluster; an upgrade to a higher Tail state still requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks in the broad Nasdaq-100 complex itself, not the overnight Asia gains, the pending data cluster, the Iran-Oman diplomatic progress, or this run's continued Alpha Vantage outage and unconfirmed live futures print.
headline: Nasdaq-100/S&P futures levels unchanged from the prior run in this run's search (stale print, no fresh intraday structure confirmed); Asia mixed-to-firm overnight (Nikkei +0.7%, Kospi +0.9%, Hang Seng -0.51%), VIX flat near 14.5-14.7, Brent little changed ~$87.18 as a reported Iran-Oman deal on Hormuz offers a mild de-escalatory signal -- today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment remain the session's main checkpoints; Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a sixth consecutive run, so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch.
body: About five minutes past the top of the hour and roughly one hour past the prior run, conditions remain calm into the European morning. This run's WebSearch results for S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures returned the identical price levels and session range as the prior run (S&P futures last ~7,825.25, range 7,773.75-7,838.50; Nasdaq 100 futures ~30,177.50, range 30,124.25-30,232.00), which is treated as a stale/cached snapshot rather than a fresh intraday print -- a genuine live price-path limitation this run, distinct from asserting the structure itself. Overnight, Asia-Pacific markets were mixed-to-firm: Nikkei 225 +0.7% and Kospi +0.9% (continued AI/semiconductor strength, Samsung/SK Hynix-linked), while Hang Seng lagged, -0.51%. This continues off Thursday's S&P 500 record close of 7,798.99 (+0.65%) on cooler PPI, with the Nasdaq Composite +0.81% and Dow +0.13% the same session. VIX holds flat near its recent range, 14.53-14.70, essentially unchanged from the prior run. Brent crude is little changed, last near $87.18 (+0.13%), as the market sits in a wait-and-see mode: a U.S. official was cited saying Iran and Oman are making progress on a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with the U.S. prepared to lift its blockade of Iranian ports once commercial shipping is fully restored -- a mild de-escalatory signal versus Thursday's framing -- though Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority publicly maintains the strait remains closed until its conditions are met, so this is progress-in-talks rather than a resolved discontinuity. The IEA reportedly cut its global oil demand outlook this week on prolonged-conflict and elevated-price concerns, a second, demand-side reason oil stays capped rather than spiking, reinforcing Stress over Tail. No fresh, index-relevant semiconductor or megacap catalyst was identified overnight: AMD's Oxford BOLD MOU and Taalas acquisition are dated Aug 12-13 and already reflected in prior runs, and Nvidia coverage continues to point to its Aug 26 earnings as the next real catalyst rather than anything overnight. Geopolitically beyond Hormuz, the Ukraine-Russia war shows no fresh market-moving escalation this run. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted for a sixth consecutive run -- the TREASURY_YIELD call was retried once and returned an immediate rate_limit error both times -- so, per the fallback protocol, this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities and price-path context; a fresh, precisely-timestamped 10-year Treasury yield print could not be confirmed this run (last reliably observed ~4.65%, unchanged). Combined with the continued Alpha Vantage outage and the stale/cached futures print, Confidence sits in the medium-low band, similar to the prior run. Tail eases marginally to 9% (still low; no persistent one-way structure evidence, and the modestly firmer overnight Asia tape is not itself a Nasdaq-100 price-path signal) while Stress eases to 26% (from 29% last run), reflecting the mildly de-escalatory Hormuz diplomatic signal and steady oil/VIX, partially offset by the approaching Retail Sales (12:30 UTC) and preliminary UMich sentiment (14:00 UTC) cluster, which remains the main driver of the forecast Stress path higher into midday UTC before easing back through the afternoon and into the next Asia handover.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-18%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft PPI; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 58%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and AMAT-earnings window before easing back into the low-to-moderate band (23-29%) by Friday's deep European morning as the after-hours reaction stayed contained to the single name and no broader transmission was confirmed.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (5-11%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to build from the high-20s toward the mid-40s across the 12:30-14:00 UTC Retail Sales / UMich sentiment cluster and the US cash-open/power-hour window before easing back through the evening and into the quiet weekend handover, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON.

forecastDetail.comment: Deep European morning: this run's search returned the same S&P/Nasdaq futures levels as the prior run -- treated as a stale print rather than fresh structure. Asia closed mixed-to-firm (Nikkei +0.7%, Kospi +0.9%, Hang Seng -0.51%); VIX flat near 14.5-14.7 and Brent little changed ~$87.18 on a reported Iran-Oman deal offering a mild de-escalatory signal versus Thursday's rhetoric.

European morning continues with thin liquidity typical of this window; no fresh Hormuz kinetic escalation or Ukraine-Russia developments identified since the prior run -- Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority continues to publicly reject the strait is open even as US-Iran-Oman diplomatic progress is reported.

London open brings modestly firmer volume; no new index-relevant semiconductor or megacap catalyst identified overnight beyond already-known Aug 12-13 AMD items, so Stress ticks up only marginally on generic session transition rather than any new information.

Late European morning holds calm; positioning ahead of the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print begins to build modestly, nudging Stress higher while Tail stays anchored in the low band absent any observed persistent one-way structure.

Final hour before Retail Sales; Stress continues to build on event positioning and forecast dispersion into the print, consistent with the framework treating pre-event anticipation as a Stress rather than Tail driver.

Retail Sales (12:30 UTC) prints within this hour, the session's first major checkpoint; Stress rises into the elevated range on event/whipsaw risk around the release, while Tail requires an observed failed-pullback/persistent-extension reaction in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself before it could follow, which is not yet asserted.
